checks.title: Scope
checks.detail: Set a time window that includes the reported incident.

checks.title: Mixed outcomes
checks.detail: Filtered ${param.incident.service} across versions and found HTTP ${param.incident.status} alongside 200 responses.

checks.title: Version comparison
checks.detail: Compared service.version with HTTP status: ${param.incident.bad_version} failed while ${param.incident.good_version} stayed healthy.

answer.evidence: HTTP ${param.incident.status} on ${param.incident.bad_version} versus 200 on ${param.incident.good_version} corroborates the version regression.

demonstration.narration:
Filter for ${param.incident.service} while keeping every service.version: ${var.query}.

We need both versions in the same result set before deciding whether the new release is unhealthy.
demonstration.reasoning:
The service and version filter removes unrelated traffic, but it does not select errors.

The http.response.status_code field supplies the outcome evidence: HTTP ${param.incident.status} is a server error, while 200 is a successful response. We need to see both here before comparing versions.
demonstration.evidence:
The filtered ${param.incident.service} results contain a mix of HTTP ${param.incident.status} and 200 in the highlighted http.response.status_code column.

The error codes show that some requests failed, but the mixed statuses mean we still need to check which service.version owns those failures before concluding that ${truth.finding} caused the regression.

inspect.narration: Add the version field as a column and compare it with HTTP response status codes across requests.

demonstration.narration:
Add service.version as a visible table column beside the existing http.response.status_code evidence.

Compare the two columns across ${param.incident.service} requests: which version returns HTTP ${param.incident.status}, and which returns 200?
demonstration.reasoning:
A version label by itself does not establish a failure. The HTTP status code tells us whether that request failed or succeeded.

Reading service.version and http.response.status_code on the same rows lets us attribute the errors to ${param.incident.bad_version} and the successful requests to ${param.incident.good_version}.
demonstration.evidence:
The highlighted columns pair ${param.incident.bad_version} with HTTP ${param.incident.status} and ${param.incident.good_version} with HTTP 200.

Those status codes are the corroborating evidence that the new version is bad, rather than the version number alone: ${truth.conclusion}
